Is there any pain or rash in or around your right ear?
Have you noticed any numbness or trouble speaking?

Have you noticed any change in taste on the front of your tongue on that side?
Do you have any changes in your hearing or any ringing in your right ear?

orders: Detailed neurological examination of all cranial nerves (specifically testing eye movements, jaw opening, palate elevation, and tongue movements)
Test for fatigable weakness - have the patient sustain upward gaze for 2 minutes and lateral gaze for 2 minutes to assess for ptosis or weakness with sustained effort
Anti-neuronal antibody panel (specifically anti-Ri, anti-Hu, and anti-CV2/CRMP5 antibodies)
Brain MRI with contrast to evaluate for structural lesions or leptomeningeal disease
CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis to screen for occult malignancy
Lumbar puncture with CSF analysis (cell count, protein, cytology, oligoclonal bands)
served: CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index

dx_raw:
The results of the anti-GQ1b, anti-GAD65 antibodies and PET/CT scan have returned:

1. Anti-GQ1b antibody: negative
2. Anti-GAD65 antibody: positive (titers elevated at 1:1000)
3. PET/CT scan: no evidence of occult malignancy

DIAGNOSIS: Opsoclonus secondary to anti-GAD65 antibody-associated autoimmune cerebellar ataxia (opsoclonus-myoclonus spectrum, idiopathic/paraneoplastic-negative variant)
